planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant once soil has warmed.

directions: Re Umberto Giallo is the golden-yellow sport of the old Italian paste tomato Re Umberto, itself named for 19th-century King Umberto I of Savoy. It sets clusters of four to five small cylindrical-to-oval fruits, occasionally with a slight pointed nipple at the blossom end, over tall indeterminate vines. The dense, paste-like flesh carries very little juice and a mild, faintly sweet flavor, making it well suited to sauces and preserves rather than fresh slicing. Growers prize its strong keeping quality; in its native Italy, whole vines were traditionally pulled in autumn and hung indoors so immature fruit could finish ripening off the plant.
